rules.title: Ban on selling or using coordinated pricing algorithms to set rents or occupancy
rules.requirement: Berkeley landlords may not use rent-pricing software that relies on non-public competitor data (less than 90 days old) to set or recommend rents or occupancy levels, and vendors may not sell such software to Berkeley landlords. A tenant whose landlord uses such software can sue for an injunction, damages, and civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation, plus attorney's fees.
rules.key_value: civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation (each month and each unit a separate violation)

coverage.summary: All residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley. The rule prohibits landlords from using coordinated pricing algorithms and prohibits selling them to Berkeley landlords.
minor_exemptions_not_in_data: Products used to set rent or income limits under government affordable housing guidelines are not covered algorithms

rules.exemptions: Excludes aggregated, anonymous rental data reports that do not recommend rents or terms; products used to set rent or income limits under government affordable housing guidelines; and market research for project financing, appraisals, and software research, testing or training (provided competitor data is not an input when a recommendation is calculated).
rules.penalty: City Attorney may sue for damages, injunctive relief, restitution, and civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation. Aggrieved tenants may sue for injunctive relief, money damages, and civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation. Each month and each unit is a separate violation. A prevailing City Attorney or tenant gets mandatory attorney's fees and costs.
rules.quoted_span:
Each separate month that a violation exists or continues, and each 
separate residential dwelling unit for which the landlord used the coordinated pricing 
algorithm, shall constitute a separate and distinct violation.
